text.tspan: Hands cultivate a garden with care.
When we care for a plant, a little care can make the experience better. Planning and thinking about
First, observing a plant helps us respond to what it needs. For example, we check whether the soil feels
dry before adding water. This is a small thing that makes the day easier.
Second, keeping a simple record helps us learn from changes. For example, we note which window
gives the plant enough light without scorching its leaves. We do not need a perfect day to do this well.
We can care for a plant more easily when we prepare and notice other people. These simple steps give
us a useful place to start.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the
conclusion. Each body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the
argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Tell a friend about a time you tried to care for a plant. What did you do? What would you change? Use four short paragraphs:
introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: say what you want to do; explain the first
step; explain a different second step; say why the two steps help.)
